structured_output.summary: Coherent ~1.2 h pulsation folds at 0.818 d; Sectors 108, 109 and prewhitening decide.
reasons: New signal: exofop_tois, exofop_ctois and published_signal are all empty, and the verification record (2026-10-17 09:16) reports no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match in the catalogues of 2026-10-16. Nothing argues for a drop on grounds of prior knowledge.

The dip is recovered independently of the QLP Sector 98 detection: other_sector_results S106 SPOC SNR 14.0 (expected 10.3) and S107 SPOC SNR 11.8 (expected 11.4); joint_search_snr 11.8 against joint_search_highest_null_snr 7.0 with joint_search_detected True; fit_depth_ppm 352 +/- 31; odd_even_difference_sigma 0.07; depth_ppm_by_sector S98 375 +/- 41, S106 265 +/- 74, S107 372 +/- 71 with sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.406.

The fitted body is planet-sized and the geometry fits a transit of the target: planet_radius_earth_radii 3.91 +/- 0.23 (far below the 22.4 stellar limit), transit_grazing False, fit_impact_parameter 0.450 +/- 0.2883, stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 1.32, fitted_to_expected_scaled_semi_major_axis 0.74; gaia_ruwe 1.16, gaia_non_single_star 0, gaia_eclipsing_binary False and gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses 0.0707 show no sign of a stellar companion, though the RV limit is weak because gaia_vbroad_km_s 270.8 gives gaia_rv_epoch_scatter_km_s 7.66.

No photometric sign of a binary in the current step-9 run: ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm 82 +/- 54 (1.5 sigma; ellipsoidal_companion_mass_solar_masses empty), secondary_depth_ppm 88 +/- 35 below secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm 107, cautions empty. The ellipsoidal caution of the 2026-10-16 00:18 run (126 +/- 31 ppm) is gone.

Main open question, which no automatic step tests: the star pulsates coherently at a frequency commensurate with the candidate period. gaia_vbroad_km_s 270.8 with stellar_radius_solar_radii 1.93 is a hot, rapidly rotating star. The all-sector figure tic121564843_0.81803.png shows oscillations of about 2000 ppm peak-to-peak with a period of about 1.2 h in all three sector panels, several times the 352 ppm dip, and in the phase-0.5 panel the S98, S106 and S107 points trace the same sinusoid in the same phase even though the sectors span about 250 days (epoch_btjd 3992.46912 to fit_epoch_btjd 4240.28625). A pulsation that folds coherently at 0.818 d over about 300 cycles has a frequency within about 0.004 c/d of a harmonic of 1/P, which is improbable by chance, so the BLS period, the 2.358 h dip (fit_duration_hours, about two pulsation cycles) and the phase-0.5 measurements may be products of multi-mode pulsation rather than of a companion. The SPOC recoveries in S106 and S107 do not exclude this because a coherent pulsation gives them the same period. A 3.91 Earth-radius body at 0.818 d around a 1.93 solar-radius star is also physically unusual, which raises the bar.

Pixel check: pixel_verdict unresolved, joint_difference_image_snr 5.4, joint_best_source Gaia DR3 2978034081419676416. In the figures, S98, S107 and S109 put the difference flux on the target pixel with the free-fit cross at or beside the target (S109 now runs and names TIC 121564843 as best star at SNR 2.2 in pixel_verdicts_by_sector); S106 and S108 are dominated by large-scale gradients and carry no position information. I disagree with the mechanical reason 'the dip can be on a nearby star': gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip says the G 18.9 star at 39 arcsec needs an 88% eclipse, which is implausible, and nfpp_mean is 0. The pixel data do not threaten the candidate; the pulsation does.

TRICERATOPS: fpp_mean 0.01284 with fpp_standard_deviation 0.026 (larger than the mean, so single runs reach about 0.04), nfpp_mean 0, most_likely_scenario TP on TIC 121564843, nearby_scenarios_excluded False. I give this little weight: it is borderline, and TRICERATOPS models only astrophysical transits or eclipses on the target or catalogued neighbours, not a pulsation-induced false alarm.

What would decide it: (a) unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star 108 109. Adding the S108 and S109 SPOC light curves to step 9 (sectors_used is 98 106 107) doubles the transit count and tests whether a 352 ppm dip persists at the propagated fit_epoch_btjd 4240.28625 and fit_period_days 0.8179751 +/- 0.00000809. cutout_depth_ppm_by_sector_and_aperture already gives S108 r1.5 11 +/- 158 and r2.0 7 +/- 163 ppm (consistent with zero and 2.1 sigma below 352) against S109 r1.5 372 +/- 183, so these sectors are suggestive but not conclusive; they would also raise joint_difference_image_snr above 5.4. (b) Prewhitening the pulsation modes in S98, S106 and S107 and repeating the search and fit: if 1/0.818 d is a harmonic or combination of the pulsation frequencies, or the dip does not survive on a flat baseline, drop; if a 352 ppm box dip survives and still appears in S108 and S109, propose for submission.

This agrees with the four earlier decisions in the verification record (2026-10-16 04:09, 04:16, 07:08 and 2026-10-17 07:57, all held) and with the mechanical 'held', but for the pulsation reason and the pending Sectors 108 and 109 rather than the nearby-star reason. Nothing has changed since 2026-10-17 except that the S109 pixel check now runs and favours the target.
